prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling through ligand control of the catalyst, which made aryl amines routine to build.
For the development of base editing: engineered deaminase chemistry that converts single DNA bases programmably without double-strand cleavage.

statement.case_for: I keep B002 with B029 and Liu alone, three people in total. B002 is the one shortlisted achievement whose effect on chemistry is already measurable in the literature: ligand design turned Pd-catalysed amination from an erratic reaction into a predictable one, and it is now routine in discovery and process chemistry and in materials, after more than 25 years of independent confirmation. The chair asked for one sentence on what is new beyond 2010. My answer is that the 2010 prize was about forming C-C bonds through transmetalation, whereas C-N coupling required control of reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes and of competing beta-hydride elimination, which was achieved by rational ligand design (bulky, electron-rich phosphines and carbenes) and is a separate mechanistic problem with its own solution. B029 is the second part because its chemical content is concrete: engineered cytidine and adenosine deaminases acting on a nucleobase in situ, with the adenine editor relying on a deaminase (evolved TadA) that has no natural counterpart for DNA. It is a different kind of achievement from B002, so the two parts do not overlap, and with Liu alone the union stays at three names.
statement.case_against: B002 can still be read as a heteroatom extension of an area honoured in 2010, and its public story is quieter than that of the biology-linked candidates. B029 comes four to six years after the 2020 CRISPR prize, long-term clinical outcomes of base-edited therapies are limited, and a Liu-only part sets aside Komor and Gaudelli, who carried out the first cytosine and adenine editor work, and Nishida and Kondo, whose Target-AID work is an earlier deaminase fusion. The pairing could also be read as a compromise between core chemistry and a fashionable topic, and a single-achievement B002 prize would be cleaner if the committee finds B029 premature or the credit unresolvable.

responses.point: Zou ranks B002 first with Buchwald and Hartwig, stresses that more than 25 years of independent confirmation leave no maturity risk, and that the Kosugi precedent must be placed in the citation or background.
responses.response: We agree on merit and on the pair, and the chair has asked us to state the new principle in one sentence. Mine: C-N coupling needed ligand-controlled reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes and suppression of beta-hydride elimination, which the C-C chemistry of 2010 did not require. I would handle Kosugi in the background text, because his tin-amide reaction was stoichiometric in toxic tin and not a general catalytic method. I am less sure than you that overlap with 2010 is a non-issue, so the citation should name ligand control and not just say Pd-catalysed C-N coupling.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, supports B029 (Liu alone) with B018 (Crews and Deshaies), and says a prize on Buchwald-Hartwig or on lipid nanoparticles would rest on more mature, more clearly chemical evidence.
responses.response: Your own case against your configuration is the argument for mine: you say B002 rests on more mature and more clearly chemical evidence, and I agree. Replacing B018 with B002 keeps your Liu-only B029 and your two-achievement structure, and removes the dependence on an approved degrader that you list as an uncertainty. On your question about the prime-editing extension (B028), I would keep it outside the citation: the base editors are the claim, and a wording limited to single-base conversion without double-strand cleavage is easier to defend. I do not think the B018 case is weak, and I would not object to it as a second part if the evidence on a degrader drug changed.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B018 first as a new pharmacological principle (E3-ligase hijacking, event-driven rather than occupancy-driven), with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and concedes that the absence of an approved drug and the omission of Ciulli are weak points.
responses.response: The principle is new and measurable, and I take your point that ternary-complex cooperativity makes it a physical-chemistry problem as well as a medicinal one. My remaining objections are the two you name yourself. First, there is no approved degrader, and for me an approval or strong late-stage data is the evidence threshold that would move B018 above B002. Second, the PROTAC and cereblon strands are in practice two discoveries, one of design and one of target identification, and a three-name cut forces either Handa or Ciulli out. I would back B018 for a later cycle with a clean Crews-Deshaies-Ciulli citation or a separate glue part.

responses.point: Chabes puts B029 first, calling base editing a defined chemical reaction made programmable, reproduced in very many laboratories, and supports giving it a clean citation with a small number of names.
responses.response: I agree that the enzymology is transparent and widely reproduced. I still hold that the citation must say what base editing adds chemically beyond the 2020 prize, and the answer is the evolved deaminases and the conversion of a base without a double-strand break, not guide-RNA targeting. On credit I have not moved from Liu alone. Komor and Gaudelli did the experimental work in Liu's group, but I cannot separate the three cleanly and the Target-AID priority claim is real, so a Liu-only part defined by the engineered base-editor concept is the most defensible within the cap. If the committee decides that three names for B029 are required, I would accept Liu, Komor and Gaudelli for B029 alone and make B002 a single-part prize.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts ligand control of C-N reductive elimination as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Whether a Liu-only B029 can be defended against the Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo claims, or whether the credit problem is serious enough to prefer a different second part.
Whether the two-part structure reads as a coherent prize or as a compromise.
Whether degrader clinical evidence (B018) will mature soon enough to displace either part.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate. I share a Lund affiliation with Heiner Linke and Emma Sparr, which does not involve any credited name. Nothing in the first-round exchange changes this disclosure.
